description:
FILED s451x (Opus agent X), from the #542 tty leg.  Residue, NOT a regression:
this shape was block-buffered before #542 too.

REPRO (needs a controlling terminal -- run it under `script -qec '...' /dev/null`):

    open(my $t, ">", "/dev/tty") or die "tty: $!";
    print $t "a\n";
    print STDOUT "S\n";
    print $t "b\n";
    close $t;

        perl  a S b          PCL  S a b

CAUSE.  #542 put every OUTPUT handle PCL builds with sb-sys:make-fd-stream
under one policy function, %p-output-buffering (fd): :line iff isatty(fd),
else :full.  A plain open does not go through it -- %p-open-impl uses CL
`open`, and SBCL's `open` has no :buffering argument (it always makes a :full
fd-stream).  So the policy reaches the standard handles, the dups and the
fork-pipe ends, and misses `open FH, ">", <a terminal>`.

perl decides this one by isatty exactly like the others (the probe above IS
the measurement: perl's $t is line-buffered on a pty).

FIX SHAPE (not designed).  Either rebuild the stream after the open when the
descriptor is a tty and the direction is output (an extra make-fd-stream on
the same fd, closing the CL stream without closing the fd -- needs care), or
stop using CL `open` for output opens and call sb-sys:make-fd-stream on an
sb-posix:open descriptor, which would also give :buffering, the append mode
and the O_* flags in one place.  The second is the real answer and is bigger
than this bug.

BAR: the repro above on a pty, plus the pipe leg unchanged (a plain open onto
a FILE is :full in both, so the whole existing Pl/t + io/ picture must be
byte-identical).

CLOSED s451z -- the BOUNDED variant, as ruled.  `%p-line-buffer-if-tty` sits on
the two OUTPUT arms of `%p-open-impl`: a NON-tty stream is handed straight
back, so the common file case is byte for byte what CL `open` produced; on a
tty the stream is rebuilt (dup the descriptor, fd-stream on the dup with
%p-output-buffering, CLOSE the original -- never merely dropped).  The full
open-path rewrite (shape 2, sb-posix:open for every mode) stays FILED.

THE HAZARD THIS TASK NAMED, MEASURED (SBCL 2.6.0) -- it does NOT reproduce:
an output fd-stream DROPPED without `close` still had a live descriptor after
two `(gc :full t)`s, and a dup outlives its original's close.  So
dup-and-close is not a workaround for a finalizer bug; it is the deterministic
shape, chosen because the alternative would depend on a finalizer's timing.
The measurement is recorded in the function's docstring so nobody re-derives
it.  Probe: /tmp scratch `fin.lisp`, two cases (drop+gc; dup then close).

BAR MET: the task's pty repro is `a S b` in perl and now `a S b` in PCL (it
was `S a b`).  NB the runner matters -- `runpcl` CAPTURES the child's stdout,
so under `script` it makes the program's STDOUT a PIPE and the measurement
reads differently; `pcl` execs and is the honest one.

Guard `Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t` 9 -> 11 rows: row 10 is the pty leg (the one
row in that file that is not a pipe -- only a terminal shows this half of the
policy; it runs under `script` and skips when script(1) is absent), row 11 the
inverse through a pipe (a plain open onto a FILE unchanged).  The file's header
note, which said the pty leg is not a gate row, is corrected.
subject: A plain `open` onto a TERMINAL block-buffers where perl line-buffers -- cl:open takes no :buffering, so the #542 policy does not reach it
